party.description: The Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand (Te Rōpu Kākāriki o Aotearoa, Niu Tīreni) is a left-wing progressive party. Its programme has historically merged climate and environmental concerns with a commitment to social justice. Founded in 1990, it has provided confidence and supply to Labour governments in 2002 and 2017. Former leader James Shaw is responsible for the Climate Change Act which commits New Zealand governments to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Chloe Swarbrick and Marama Davidson are the co-leaders of the Green Party. Its slogan in 2026 is “For All of Us.”

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that multi-national businesses send profits offshore and don't pay the same taxes as local businesses. This increases prices and decreases wages. Lower corporate taxes have not led to improvements for working New Zealanders. The corporate tax rate increase would only be on the 0.7 percent biggest businesses in NZ, including banks, supermarkets and energy companies. This would level the playing field for small and medium businesses.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase the tax rate to 33% for large corporations while keeping it at 33% for small and medium businesses. A bank levy of 0.06 percent would be added to the liabilities of the four big banks (ANZ, BNZ, Westpac and ASB).

attributes.value: This party says that the richest 311 households in NZ pay an effective tax rate of 9 percent, half that of most working people. This is because much of this wealth sits in asset portfolios, rather than being taxed as income. The wealthy need to contribute to solving shared problems with the rest of New Zealand. With the 150 richest people in NZ holding as much as 917,000 households, it is important to ensure the wealthy contribute through taxes.

attributes.name: How

The profit from the sale is applied to the seller’s annual personal income and taxed at the marginal income tax rate.  The family home would be exempt.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that synthetic nitrogen fertiliser is harming our environment by polluting our rivers, lakes and groundwater. Between 1991 and 2019, the use of synthetic nitrogen increased by more than 600%. At the same time, more than a third of monitored groundwater sources saw an increase in nitrate levels. It says that contamination of community water supplies poses a risk to human health.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would lower the current cap on synthetic nitrogen fertiliser for the dairy industry. This is because the dairy industry uses more than 60% of synthetic nitrogen. It would work with farmers across other sectors to cut fertiliser. There is no timeframe set for the phase-out. It would work alongside the Ministry for Primary Industries to develop a clear implementation plan with milestones and would support regenerative farming initiatives such as the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures fund.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that this policy would help make household power bills more affordable so people would not have to choose between heating or eating. This party says that since 2021, 100,000 more households cannot afford to heat their home and 76,000 could not pay their bills on time. The easiest way to lower household power is to help people generate and store solar power but most people are barred from this due to the expensive upfront cost of equipment purchase.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would establish a government-backed loan scheme to enable zero-interest clean energy loans for up to 90% of homeowners. Homeowners can use these loans for rooftop solar, batteries and making energy efficiency upgrades. Some borrowers will have the option to defer repayments until property sale, while loans will be paid off over time via a separate levy. Central government would be a 20 percent shareholder, with participating councils and the Local Government Funding Agency (LGFA) splitting the remaining 80 percent. The Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA) would implement the scheme.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ needs a resilient energy system to provide backup renewable power that keeps electricity affordable when hydro lakes are low and wind power decreases. Gas historically fills this gap, but gas is being exhausted more quickly than expected.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create Kiwipower, a new publicly owned Crown entity that invests in renewable energy generation. Its main focus would be on renewable firming capacity such as geothermal, batteries, demand response, biomass and pumped hydro, to ensure energy demands can be met at all times. Kiwipower would contract firming capacity and make that capacity available to independent generators, retailers and energy users at affordable and transparent prices. Large power companies would be required to provide a portion of their firming capacity to Kiwipower. The entity would be funded by a tax on the wealthy, at an estimated cost $980m over four years.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that marae are a key part of New Zealand's national identity for Māori and non-Māori. They are a central hub during states of emergency, serving and connecting communities. Despite this significance, marae across NZ are ageing with failing infrastructure and need long-term financial support to be sustained.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create Te Rangatiratanga Trust, which provides immediate support and long-term funding certainty for marae, owned and operated by hapū and iwi. The Crown would provide $2.44bn to establish the trust and two funds: Te Rākau Whakarauora Restoration Fund, which would provide $400m over four years for urgent needs, and Te Tōtara Haemata Intergenerational Fund, to protect and grow capital for future generations. The latter would be funded by returns from a $2bn diversified portfolio. Trust funding decisions would be made independently of ministers and successive governments.

attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand's unique biodiversity is particularly vulnerable to the negative impact of invasive species, pollution and disease such as Kauri dieback and myrtle rust.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund research to understand diseases that affect indigenous species and establish strategies to combat the spread of these diseases.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand's biodiversity has evolved uniquely, which means our indigenous species are particularly vulnerable to extinction and human pressures, including genetic bottlenecks.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would research and monitor genetic bottlenecks and inbreeding depression in indigenous species. It would fund genetic rescue programmes to increase genetic variation, establish genome and seed banks for indigenous species and explore ways to use eco-sourcing in nurseries and re-wilding programmes.

attributes.name: How

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that indigenous forests provide a home and habitat to many of New Zealand's native fauna. Protecting these forests will ensure the whole ecosystem can thrive.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would strengthen the existing restrictions and penalties on the harvesting and export of indigenous logs and chips, including swamp kauri. It would ensure that any removal of windthrown trees on public conservation land is ecologically and culturally sound. It would also prioritise the control of introduced pests that contribute to forest collapse (i.e. possums, pigs, and deer) over recreational hunting.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says conservation has become disconnected from, and is failing to uphold, Te Tiriti o Waitangi. This is further distancing Māori from their ancestral lands and undermining their kaitiaki guardian role of looking after the environment. Te ao Māori principles can help all New Zealanders better care for their environment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure all environmental protection and resource management legislation reflects Te Tiriti o Waitangi and Māori cultural values, and upholds the tino rangatiratanga of iwi and hapū to protect their environment. In cooperation with local government, this policy would also ensure conservation efforts uphold kaitiaki through enabling customary use of indigenous resources and implementing the recommendations of the Ko Aotearoa Tēnei Waitangi Tribunal (WAI262) report. It would recognise native species as tāonga, Māori treasures, and increase public awareness of the colonial history of public conservation land, and how Te Tiriti o Waitangi and conservation intersect.

attributes.value: This party says that despite decades of conservation efforts across New Zealand, biodiversity is continuing to decline.

attributes.name: How

It would also enable the purchase, protection and regeneration of special places that are threatened in the public conservation estate and strengthen the role of conservation boards as individual advocates representing the community. Community efforts to regenerate urban biodiversity would also be supported, with funding increased for evidence-based landscape-scale conservation projects.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that climate change is damaging Māori customary practices, cultural identity, well-being and connection to the land. Historical and current injustices have also weakened the resources of Māori communities and businesses to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would ensure Māori communities and leadership networks are resourced to research, monitor and provide advice on climate change on policies and legislation that might negatively affect them. It would also fund Māori-led initiatives for transitioning away from fossil fuel and agribusiness ventures into sustainable industries. 
This policy would ensure overarching support for the autonomy and self-determination of hapū, iwi and Māori businesses in leading their own climate change responses, with funding provided to redress inequities.

policies.statement: Support Māori autonomy in their responses to climate change

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the overarching legislation for addressing climate change is too weak to actually prevent the negative impacts we are seeing and will see more in the future. Large, profit-driven corporations are influencing decision-makers reducing the voice of individuals and communities. NZ's dependence on fossil fuel is also deeply embedded in all parts of our economy, which is a barrier to economic resilience and limits the effectiveness of climate policies.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would require the implementation of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and co-governance in decision-making and extend the Climate Change Response Act to cover every sector and all greenhouse gases. 
Domestic air and shipping fuel emissions would also be included in calculating emissions for both the public and private sectors. Non-forestry carbon sequestration technologies would be on a pathway to net carbon-zero, and emission reduction targets would be transparent and align with global obligations. Purchases of offshore emissions credits would be allowed only as a last resort. There would be robust monitoring and enforcement of the legal obligations for emissions reduction contained in the Act.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the overarching legislation for addressing climate change is not strong enough to prevent the negative impacts we are seeing and will see more in the future. Economic activity, linked to greenhouse gas emissions, is prioritised over the voices of the community.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would set legally binding emission reduction targets across regions and sectors that align with the national Emission Reduction Plans. Local governments would be held accountable for meeting their responsibilities under the Climate Change Response Act and Māori communities would be empowered to implement their own climate adaption plans, as well as co-design carbon-negative economic strategies. The party would also promote research and development into fossil fuel alternatives, improve coordination of climate mitigation and adaptation activities and ensure the NZ public have access to the latest climate change-related evidence.

policies.statement: Enforce timely and effective implementation of climate legislation

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the overarching legislation for addressing climate change is not strong enough to prevent the negative impacts we are seeing and will see more in the future. Economic activity, linked to greenhouse gas emissions, is prioritised over the voices of the community.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure the Emissions Trading Scheme is sufficient to meet reduction obligations under the Climate Change Response Act and can compensate for climate change mitigation and adaptation costs. The scheme must be consistent with the Climate Change Commission's advice and incentivise gross rather than net emissions reductions. It would phase out the free allocation of units, removing forestry offsetting so the system functions as a genuine ‘cap-and-trade’ system, and redirect funding from the reformed ETS to an improved Government Investment in Decarbonising Industry Fund.

policies.statement: Focus on reducing gross emissions, rather than net emissions

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that all sectors need to be incentivised to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions, in order to prioritise the health of the environment and humanity over profit.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would phase out the free allocation of NZUs to emission-Intensive and trade-exposed industries, and implement a framework for pricing agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. It would also include emissions from international aviation in pricing schemes. Marine-based 'blue carbon' - carbon dioxide captured and stored by the world's ocean and coastal ecosystems - would be included in the ETS. Alternative emissions pricing mechanisms would be implemented when the ETS is not doing its job in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Lastly, existing foresters would received equitable treatment from any changes in forestry-related carbon offsetting systems.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that New Zealand has a legal and moral responsibility, supported by the Te Tiriti o Waitangi, to lead climate action on a global scale. New Zealand is relatively wealthy but currently ranks poorly against other countries for its climate change policies. This party says we need to do better to help our vulnerable neighbours, like Pacific Island nations.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would advocate internationally for the strengthening of international climate agreements and encourage all countries to increase their Nationally Determined Contributions so that global emissions halve by 2030 and reach net carbon-negative by 2050 to limit global average temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius. The party would also advocate for urgent climate action to be embedded in all international agreements and institutions, with a legally binding mechanism created to ensure international compliance with climate commitments and ramped-up funding made available to finance climate adaptation around the world. It would promote that decisions are led by Indigenous leadership and countries and communities particularly vulnerable to climate change.

attributes.value: This party says that both climate change and the necessary actions needed to mitigate and adapt to its negative consequences threaten to worsen socioeconomic inequalities. In moving towards a carbon-negative economy, people who work in high-emission industries may lose their jobs.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund free vocational training and redeployment opportunities for those in high-emission industries to transition to climate-safe work. It would also provide access to redundancy compensation for people working in sectors that are adversely affected by climate change mitigation and adaptation actions.

attributes.value: This party says that climate change adaptation measures must be adopted by all of New Zealand, meaning everyone needs to work together from the government down to the individual.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase resourcing and accountability for climate adaptation within local government, including providing additional resources to those lease resourced to take climate action. It would also prioritise long-term, nature-based solutions aligned with tikanga Māori and culturally appropriate values and ensure every student knows how to respond and stay hopeful in the face of climate change. This party would also expand the role of the Natural Hazards Commission to include cover for climate-related weather events and ensure it plays a key role in managing community-led adaptation and retreat.

Central and local governments must provide support for their communities to proactively plan and adapt.

attributes.name: How

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that by urgently phasing out fossil fuels, NZ can ease the cost of living pressures and reduce our country's vulnerability to global price shocks. To do this, NZ needs to be led by strong domestic targets that stop emissions at the source and make polluting corporations pay.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require the government Budget process to be consistent with limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees, gross emissions-reduction targets, and international commitments.  It would also improve public transparency on the costs of inaction by including the fiscal impact of the Nationally Determined Contribution obligation in the financial statements.

policies.statement: Increase the reporting and transparency aspects of the Zero Carbon Act

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that governance of the agricultural sector should recognise the expertise and rights of Māori and have self-governance over mahinga kai (food production). The agriculture sector and regional councils should work in partnership with Māori, in line with Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would implement the recommendations of the Waitangi Tribunal to ensure that governance of the agricultural sector upholds Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

policies.statement: Implement Waitangi Tribunal recommendations to ensure governance of the agricultural sector upholds Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says governance of the agricultural sector should recognise the expertise and rights of Māori and have self-governance over mahinga kai (traditional food gathering practices). The agriculture sector and regional councils should work in partnership with Māori, in line with Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support Māori to address barriers found in banking, tax, company and co-operative laws that prevent te ao Māori principles from being applied to the production of food and fibre and/or Māori land use and development.

policies.statement: Support Māori to address barriers to traditional food production

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand needs strong agricultural standards to ensure it remains known for its premium-quality and environmentally sustainable products.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would establish an Agricultural Standards Framework that includes requirements to measure all agricultural inputs and outputs, and robust and consistent measures of environmental impacts caused by agriculture. The framework would also include sustainability standards for all food and fibre sectors and incentives and other support to farmers to continuously improve ecosystems on productive land.

policies.statement: Establish an Agricultural Standards Framework

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand needs strong agricultural standards to ensure it remains known for its environmentally sustainable products. NZ should not import products known for their link to tropical deforestation and habitat loss.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would prohibit palm kernel expeller (PKE) imports. This is a solid by-product left over from extracting oil from the seeds of oil palm fruit.

policies.statement: Prohibit palm kernel expeller (PKE) imports

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealanders should be able to swim in unpolluted rivers and lakes. However, nitrogen fertilisers used on farms are polluting our freshwater. Fossil fuels are used in the production of nitrogen fertiliser, contributing to the climate emergency.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would impose nitrogen caps on all agricultural practices, and it would also prohibit the production of nitrogenous fertilisers from fossil fuels.

policies.statement: Impose nitrogen caps on all agricultural practices

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that New Zealand should be working to look after its environment so that its communities and biodiversity are sustained. Allowing animals to graze on conservation land is prioritising economic opportunities over the core purpose of conservation land: preserving and protecting our native ecosystems.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would phase out most grazing concessions on public conservation land and require sustainable farm plans for active concessions.

policies.statement: Phase out most grazing concessions on public conservation land

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ should be working to look after its environment so that its communities and indigenous biodiversity are sustained.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support farmers in sensitive ecosystems to work collaboratively to protect indigenous biodiversity.

policies.statement: Support farmers in sensitive ecosystems to work collaboratively to protect indigenous biodiversity

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the agriculture industry in New Zealand should be working to positively contribute to clean air and a safe climate. To do this, all agricultural businesses must work together to achieve a significant cut in gross emissions.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would adjust stocking rates according to the holding capacity of the land, protect existing wetlands and encourage wetland restoration, phase out the use of fossil fuels for agricultural processes, and phase out synthetic nitrogen fertilisers. It would also require the agriculture sector to provide data that enables greenhouse gas emissions to be measured and incentivise low greenhouse gas agricultural initiatives.

policies.statement: Reduce agricultural emissions in New Zealand

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that to protect New Zealand's food and agricultural products for generations to come, the agricultural sector needs to become resilient, diversified and agile. It will continue to face changing weather patterns, markets, and consumer demands.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require imported foods to meet our own national growing and production requirements and support a transition to agroecological practices (such as regenerative and organic approaches). It would also encourage preserving and growing heritage seeds for personal use and commercial production and strengthen the collective resilience of grassroots community collaborations like local catchment groups.

policies.statement: Create a resilient agricultural sector

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that communities benefit from local and seasonal produce that is nutritious, safe, fresh, and affordable. We should be supporting innovative agricultural practices and systems that encourage a thriving sector.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would provide startup funding for innovative systems and/or new food and fibre trials, and fund ongoing research to explore sustainable agricultural livelihoods that require less energy, time and costs. It would also provide resources for projects addressing the food and fibre needs of local communities.

policies.statement: Provide resources and funding for innovative agricultural projects

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that in meeting New Zealand's commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, mātauranga Māori must be recognised, and Māori communities should be supported to grow, forage and hunt for food on their land.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would prioritise iwi-based initiatives in the management and restoration of retired and/or degraded agricultural land. It would fund research and development that supports hapū and iwi, Māori agribusiness and resources. A Māori-led authority would be set up to oversee the distribution of start-up funding for locally-led and sustainable Māori agricultural initiatives.

policies.statement: Honour traditional Māori agricultural practices

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that animals in New Zealand's agricultural industry should enjoy the highest animal welfare standards. Welfare standards need to be properly enforced so that any animal death is managed as humanely as possible.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ban the importation of animals and animal products when living conditions in their country of origin have not met Aotearoa New Zealand’s animal welfare standards and would empower resource animal welfare inspectors and prosecutors to fully uphold the Animal Welfare Act. It would also address the requirements of the Global Animal Protection Index to improve animal welfare in New Zealand, and prohibit new, and phase out existing factory farming of animals, including highly intensive outdoor facilities like feedlots. Transport standards that are fit-for-purpose and animal-focused would be adopted.

policies.statement: Ensure the agricultural industry uses an ethical and human approach to animal management

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that animals have the right to good nutrition and a safe and happy environment. They are due respect and love, and humans have a duty of care towards animals they interact with. They should not be violated or exploited, and their distress and pain should be minimised.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure that the Animal Welfare Act 1999 and other related legislation are fit for purpose, evidence-based, and enforced, aligning Codes of Welfare with the Act. It would also establish a Department of Animal Welfare, led by a Minister for Animal Welfare and a Parliamentary Commissioner for Animal Justice, and resource it to investigate and make recommendations on animal welfare issues. Local governments would be adequately resourced to uphold and monitor Animal Welfare bylaws. It would also develop codes of welfare for home kills and support animals.

policies.statement: Ensure New Zealand's legal system upholds an animal's right to a life worth living

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that humans have a duty of care towards animals they interact with. They should not be violated or exploited, and their distress and pain should be minimised.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create national standards for the registered breeding of companion animals and limit the number of litters an individual animal can have over a lifetime. People who breed companion animals for sale and rescue centres must register and hold a current licence. It would also review the appropriateness of breed-specific legislation, and ban breeding of lineages with high susceptibility to genetic welfare issues.

policies.statement: Create national standards for the registered breeding of companion animals

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that people have a duty of respect for animals' rights. They should not be violated or exploited, and their distress and pain should be minimised.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would limit the number of companion animals an individual can have at once, with pathways for exemptions, such as for owners who can demonstrate being able to uphold welfare. It would implement codes of welfare for highly social animals, such as guinea pigs, rabbits, birds, rats, goats, horses and pigs, that require them to always be kept with others of their species. The party would also ban prolonged close confinement of animals and amend the Residential Tenancies Act 1986 to ensure that renters are able to own a registered companion or support animal when the animal meets local bylaws.

policies.statement: Implement improved welfare regulations for companion animals

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says humans have an ethical obligation to make informed decisions on behalf of animals, drawing on the best available knowledge of their needs and behaviours. This includes tikanga and mātauranga Māori.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reform animal welfare legislation to recognise Māori concepts and values, in partnership with tāngata whenua, and ensure Māori representation on decision-making bodies for animal welfare. It would establish a Department of Animal Welfare, led by a Minister for Animal Welfare.

policies.statement: Ensure animal welfare regulations upholds Te Tiriti o Waitangi and incorporates Māori cultural values

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that we need to carefully balance the needs of indigenous species and introduced animals. Indigenous species and ecosystems are essential for maintaining ecological balance, so their interests should be prioritised over invasive species.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would develop local regulations around pet ownership to cater for the indigenous species residing in that locale, such as requiring catios to keep cats safe and protect local biodiversity. This includes funding free spaying and neutering for pets, introducing national standards for desexing dogs and registering, desexing and microchipping cats, and regulating recreational activities like hunting and fishing when they negatively affect indigenous species.

policies.statement: Reform animal welfare legislation so that it protects indigenous biodiversity

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the government has a responsibility to protect Māori interests, work in partnership with Māori, and respect Māori autonomy in disasters.  Decisions made during emergencies should also respect local knowledge.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would guarantee Māori representation at all levels of emergency management planning. It would formalise the role of iwi and hapū Māori in risk reduction, adaptation and recovery. It would also invest in the capacity and capability of iwi and hapū to respond in emergencies, and resource rural marae that want to be autonomous hubs for emergency preparedness and response.

policies.statement: Uphold the leadership of Māori during emergency management

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand faces certain and increasing threats of many kinds, both natural and man-made.  Looking after the natural world is critical for minimising the risks and impacts of emergencies.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would set nature-based hazard mitigation as the default approach to hazard mitigation, but only if that approach does not negatively impact people and communities. The emergency response approach should be flexible and outcome- and needs-oriented, preserving local ecosystems, tikanga, and communities. To ensure this, the party would standardise Fire and Emergency NZ's chemical, biological, radioactive and nuclear response procedures and prepare a rapid, coordinated response plan covering marine emergencies and the impacts of land-based emergencies on the marine environment.

policies.statement: Make nature-based solutions the primary mechanism for hazard mitigation

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand faces certain and increasing threats of many kinds, both natural and man-made. The government should provide the financial, material and training resources that agencies and community organisations require to effectively plan for and respond to emergencies of all kinds.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund critical roles and equipment for all emergency response services, including energy and communications providers, so they can prepare to maintain service resilience in emergencies. Stockpiles and systems providing lifesaving supplies would be organised in local and regional hubs, with regional preparedness plans created. Community organisations would receive training in emergency response, with multilingual, community-led education about emergency preparation and response for the public. It would also fund scientific research on resilience, risk mitigation, and adaptation and funding for locally led long-term recovery work with public engagement on who pays for this.

policies.statement: Adequately resource national, regional and local emergency systems so communities are prepared for future emergencies.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that all people should be empowered to pre-emptively shape the emergency management systems that affect them through community engagement enabled by good evidence, co-design, and adequate resourcing.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would prioritise collaborative plans and strategies for targeted support towards communities at risk, including isolated people or communities, people at risk, and marginalised groups. It would ensure these communities were supported through developing and resourcing individualised preparedness plans. This would include providing tailored emergency preparedness and response information in various formats and languages to communities and households.

policies.statement: Take a preventative approach regarding emergency management responses

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that emergency management should prioritise basic needs and restoring essential services. Emergency financial support systems should maintain basic living standards and avoid exacerbating existing inequities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would set minimum standards for regional resilience in critical utilities, including the electrical grid and satellite communications and provide resources to remote communities so they can establish local alternatives to these centralised critical systems. It would also provide easily accessible basic resources as needed, including food, shelter, repairs, and clothing,  regardless of people’s immediate ability to pay.

policies.statement: Prioritise making critical utilities resilient in preparation for future emergencies

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that food is deeply connected to wellbeing, culture, identity, and the health of the planet. By restoring Māori-led kaitiakitanga of mahinga kai and prioritising nutritious, sustainable food systems, we can strengthen relationships with the environment and support healthier communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support learning opportunities for children and communities to grow, harvest, prepare, and share nutritious wholefoods through school gardens and food education programmes. It would strengthen Māori-led approaches to caring for mahinga kai and ensure traditional knowledge and practices are valued and supported. A national whole food system strategy will guide decision-making by honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi and prioritising the health of people and the planet alongside sustainable practices.

policies.statement: Support Māori led education for growing and preparing food

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says food security and sovereignty are essential for the health, wellbeing, and resilience of communities. It believes all consumers should have agency over their food and be able to make informed choices. There should also be a wide range of options close to where people live so they can choose nourishing food that meets their cultural needs.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support tangata whenua-led food production, distribution, and decision-making processes It would protect and promote foods and practices that reflect mana whenua (the people of the land). This party would work to ensure consumers have access to clear, accurate information about the nutritional, environmental, and ethical impacts of food choices. It would revise relevant legislation to protect the human right to be free from hunger and malnutrition.

policies.statement: Support access to food security and traditional food practices

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that access to nourishing food is essential for people’s health, well-being, and ability to participate fully in society. A food system therefore should support communities by reducing food insecurity, strengthenen local connections, and ensuring that healthy choices are available to everyone.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support community food hubs, distribution programmes, and local food initiatives that improve access to fresh and nutritious foods. It would address unfair practices within the grocery sector through stronger legislation that promotes competition and fairness. Actions would also focus on making nourishing foods and drinks more affordable and accessible.

policies.statement: Ensure everyone has reliable access to affordable, fresh, and nutritious food

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our children and young people deserve to be loved, nurtured and safe. We have a shared responsibility to make sure tamariki's voices are heard, centred and reflected in all decisions that impact them.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create and amend legislation so that the child’s voice is central in all decisions that matter to them. It would do this by using the Child Impact Assessment Tool consistently in all government policy and planning, and fully incorporating the Rights of the Child into legislation.

policies.statement: Make a child's voice central in all decisions that matter to them

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our children and young people deserve to be loved, nurtured and safe. We have a shared responsibility to make sure children are free from poverty as soon as they are born.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase the Best Start payment and extend it to every child under three as a universal child benefit for the early years.

policies.statement: Make the Best Start payment for children universal

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that children and young people deserve a skilled, well-supported workforce that is trauma-informed, culturally responsive and properly trained when dealing with their safety, health and education.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would would fund training and create a workforce development strategy. This would prioritise Māori, Pacific, rainbow, disabled and community provider pathways.

policies.statement: Improve workforce safety in the child protection system

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that children deserve to be supported in each of their unique journeys through life. A functioning society should ensure children with disabilities or learning support needs get the help they need to have a great quality of life.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would improve access to both diagnosis and support services for children with disabilities or learning support needs.

policies.statement: Improve access for diagnosis services for children with disabilities or learning support needs

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that young Māori children are disproportionately impacted by New Zealand's current child protection system. This is because it excludes meaningful partnership and underinvests in culturally grounded, whānau-led solutions. The party says that to uphold our commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, we need to address the inequities tamariki Māori face in everyday life and in the state care system.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would amend the Oranga Tamariki Act to protect tamariki Māori and explicitly embed whānau participation in decision-making to exercise iwi or hapū authority. It would implement the Waitangi Tribunal recommendations regarding Oranga Tamariki.

policies.statement: Amend the Oranga Tamariki Act to explicitly protect Māori children

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealand's flora and fauna are central to our national identity and way of life. Yet they are often threatened by economic goals, as well as introduced predators. This party says that conservation decisions should be made for the public good, not in the interests of private profiteers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase overall public conservation funding, including increasing funding and support for the Predator Free 2050 goal.

policies.statement: Increase overall public conservation funding

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that artists and creatives deserve to be valued, respected and recognised for their work. Yet currently, too many are without the certainty of a stable income, and many lack access to the training and education needed to foster their skills and talents. Creatives should be supported in their work.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require that all publicly funded projects pay at least the living wage to artists and expand paid artist residencies so creatives can upskill and grow their practice while building a meaningful livelihood.

policies.statement: Require all publicly funded projects to pay at least the living wage to artists

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that artists and creatives deserve to be valued, respected and recognised for their work. Yet currently, too many are without the certainty of a stable income. Creatives should be supported in their practice and provided opportunities to participate in events where they can grow and showcase their work.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would provide stable funding for creative organisations and events such as Te Urungi, including long-term funding for significant creative initiatives such as Te Matatini and Polyfest.

policies.statement: Provide stable funding for creative organisations and events

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that artists and creatives deserve to be valued, respected and recognised for their work. Yet currently, too many are without the certainty of a stable income. Creatives should be supported in their practice and provided opportunities to participate in events where they can grow and showcase their work.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would provide sustainable long-term arts funding that is not reliant on gambling revenue, alongside alcohol-free venues for performers.

policies.statement: Provide long-term arts funding for creatives

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that repatriation of items of cultural significance is an act of reconciliation, restoring dignity to ancestors taken illegally from iwi and hapū during the colonial era. These taonga are part of New Zealand's cultural identity and should live within its shores.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would invest in repatriating taonga currently overseas back to iwi, hapū and whānau Māori, as well as keeping taonga in NZ.

policies.statement: Support the repatriation of taonga overseas back to the Māori community

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that arts, culture and creativity are vital for creating vibrant cities and communities. Like other community infrastructure, the arts, culture and creative sectors need proper support.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would establish infrastructure across ministries to strengthen our creative and cultural economy and maximise opportunities for local artists.

policies.statement: Establish infrastructure across ministries to strengthen our creative and cultural economy

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that non-commercial public media can nurture and promote our talent and creativity as a nation, providing original opportunities without the need to prioritise profit.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase funding for quality, non-commercial public media, including sustainable funding for Radio New Zealand and Whakaata Māori.

policies.statement: Increase funding for non-commercial public media

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that young people and local communities deserve opportunities to foster their skills and talents in media and radio. This promotes culture and creativity that is vital for creating vibrant cities and communities, alongside encouraging young New Zealanders to grow their careers in the country.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund and resource student, community, regional, Māori and Pacific media and radio.

policies.statement: Increase funding for community media

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that te reo Māori is a national treasure and initiatives that help it thrive should be supported so future generations can learn and enjoy the language. Supporting te reo Māori also supports whānau, hapū and iwi to be connected to their culture.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund an additional $50m towards te reo Māori initiatives each year. This would be made up of: $30m a year to programmes that provide continuous education and professional development for teachers in te reo Māori, and $20m a year towards increased funding for Te Taura Whiri and Te Mātāwai.

citations.title: 'Ake, Ake, Ake: Green Party commits $200m to the future of te reo Māori', 14 September 2026 (accessed 14 September 2026)

policies.statement: Provide $200m towards te reo Māori initiatives

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that democracy in New Zealand should uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi and the vision of Matike Mai Aotearoa, creating a decision-making process that reflects genuine partnership.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would resource a national conversation for constitutional change that upholds He Whakaputanga (the Declaration of Independence of the United Tribes of New Zealand) and Te Tiriti o Waitangi as our founding constitutional documents, utilising Matike Mai Aotearoa to facilitate community discussions.

policies.statement: Resource a national conversation for constitutional change

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that expanding voting rights creates a more representative democracy where everyone's voices are respected and heard.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would uphold the right to vote by extending the voting age to 16, extending the right to vote to all people in custody and restoring enrolment up to election day.

policies.statement: Expand voting rights in New Zealand

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that democracy in New Zealand needs to represent our entire population. It should appreciate Te Tiriti o Waitangi as a decision-making process that reflects a genuine partnership.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would entrench the Māori electoral seats to guarantee Māori representation in Parliament and extend the time in which Māori can switch rolls.

policies.statement: Entrench the Māori electoral seats

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that democracy should work for everyone, not just those who are wealthy. The richest few can currently spend millions of dollars backing different political parties and ministers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would limit donations to registered voters, increase public financing of campaigns and cap a donor’s donations at a level that does not risk donor influence over policy.

policies.statement: Reform electoral funding policies

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the wealthiest few in New Zealand have the resources to influence government policies and decisions through political lobbying. Yet this excludes the rest of the country from advocating for the issues that matter most to them.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would strengthen the rules and transparency over political lobbying, through creating a lobbyist register and a code of conduct.

policies.statement: Strengthen political lobbying rules

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that digital environments need to support our wellbeing, especially for young social media users who are often more vulnerable in the digital space.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would introduce a Digital Duty of Care to address harmful content and behaviour on social media platforms. This would require algorithmic transparency and accessible and responsive complaints systems, as well as strengthening enforcement with an independent national regulator.

policies.statement: Regulate social media platforms to address harmful content

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that digitial platforms should be held accountable for protecting the public and its information. This party believes a harm-reduction approach should be taken to digital technology.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would regulate artificial intelligence to ensure its use is safe, transparent and accurate. It would also create stricter rules around "deepfakes" and scam material.

policies.statement: Regulate artificial intelligence to limit the harm from scams and deepfakes

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that multinational tech giants are part of New Zealand's digital infrastructure. However, they are not adequately regulated, meaning profits are going overseas rather than back into the New Zealand economy.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would crack down on tax avoidance and the offshoring of profits by multinational tech giants such as Meta, Amazon and Microsoft.

policies.statement: Crack down on tax avoidance by offshore corporations

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that without the regulation of AI models, Māori culture is being exploited and stolen by overseas platforms.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would adopt and implement the Māori Data Governance Model and Māori AI Governance Framework from Te Kāhui Raraunga across the public sector to protect Māori data sovereignty.

policies.statement: Protect Māori data sovereignty

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that the companies that are holding public data, including health biometrics and personal information, cannot always be trusted to protect it.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would strengthen obligations on data-holders to protect user and biometric data by increasing penalties for privacy breaches, and strengthen the Privacy Commissioner's enforcement powers to protect personal information better.

policies.statement: Strengthen obligations for data-holders to protect user data

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that digital environments should support our wellbeing, yet many young people have been exposed to harmful and toxic content. We should equip our young people with adequate tools so they can use digital technologies without compromising their privacy and online safety and keep up with the rapid development of technology.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would expand media and digital literacy education to equip New Zealanders to navigate AI-generated media and other emerging digital technologies.

policies.statement: Expand media and digital literacy education

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that in NZ, there is a great digital divide, which only increases inequalities. Every person should be able to access the digital infrastructure necessary to actively participate and thrive in society.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reduce barriers to digital inclusion by ensuring all communities have access to the internet, have suitable devices and have offline alternatives for essential services.

policies.statement: Reduce barriers to digital inclusion

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that disabled people are often denied the same rights as others. They can also be excluded from places and activities that non-disabled people take for granted. These barriers are often worse for tāngata whaikaha Māori.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would introduce a disability rights law based on Te Tiriti with enforceable accessibility standards. Policy-makers would need to collaboratively design laws, policies, and systems in ways that work for disabled people.

policies.statement: Create a disability rights law based on Te Tiriti o Waitangi

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that in New Zealand, disabled people are often denied the same rights as others. They can also be excluded from places and activities that non-disabled people take for granted. All disabled people deserve enough support so that they can participate equally in life and in their communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would provide easily accessible and timely income support to meet all disability-related living and medical costs. This income support would be regardless of relationship status and cause of disability.

policies.statement: Provide accessible and timely income support for disabled people

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our current laws, policies and social norms mean disabled people are often denied the same rights as others. They are often excluded from places and activities non-disabled people take for granted, such as the basic human right to shelter.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would address homelessness and work towards ensuring all disabled people can live in safe, accessible, affordable housing in the community of their choice, including by setting robust universal design standards for public and private housing. Institutional group home settings would be phased out.

policies.statement: Ensure all disabled people can access and live in safe housing

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our current laws, policies and social norms mean disabled people are often denied the same rights as others. They are often excluded from places and activities non-disabled people take for granted, such as accessing public transport and travelling around their communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would make getting around accessible through continuing to fund the 75% subsidy for the Total Mobility taxi scheme, making it easier to use and increasing the number of mobility vehicles to meet demand.

policies.statement: Make travel accessible for disabled people

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our current laws, policies and social norms mean disabled people are often denied the same rights as others. They are often excluded from places and activities non-disabled people take for granted, such as accessing public transport, basic health care and inclusive education. Interactions with public services should effectively support disabled people's wellbeing.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would remove barriers to accessing the essentials like health care, transport, inclusive education and disability support for all who need it. The party would do this by drawing on the Enabling Good Lives approach as a guide to how government agencies work with disabled people. It would provide public service staff with resourcing and training to meet access needs and counter ableism and operate using a high-trust model that recognises disabled people as experts in their own lives, while making support and services available when needed.

policies.statement: Remove barriers to accessing essential services for disabled people

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that disabled people are often more vulnerable than non-disabled people during emergencies. It does not want disabled people to be left behind in times of emergency. Their needs must be considered and supported.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would resource a coordinated approach to disability in emergency management, including a national disability emergency management strategy. It would prioritise disabled input and leadership locally and nationally within emergency response planning and communication.

policies.statement: Ensure national and local emergency response plans address the needs of disabled people

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone, with the support of people of their own choosing when appropriate, should have autonomy and equal recognition before the law. Disabled people, like others should be in charge of decisions about our own lives.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would uphold legal capacity for everyone, moving from legal capacity assessments to rights-based systems of supported decision-making. This includes disabled people and their families being able to rely on accessible, timely, and affordable healthcare, mental health support and palliative care, without fear of judgement.

policies.statement: Uphold legal capacity for everyone in New Zealand

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that drugs exist and people use them. This party wants to reduce harm that can arise from drug use by taking a health-based approach rather than a punitive approach to drug use. Drug criminalisation leads to unsafe drug use, fosters organised crime, and traps those convicted in a cycle of poverty that, in turn, contributes to harmful drug use.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would repeal and replace the Misuse of Drugs Act with an evidence-based approach that reduces harm, treats drug use as a health issue and provides for regulated access to cannabis for personal use. As a short-term measure, it would implement the recommendations of the Law Commission’s 2011 review of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1975. The new Act would be co-designed with Māori under a Te Tiriti o Waitangi framework and would promote the rights and interests of whānau, hapū, and iwi.

policies.statement: Repeal and replace the Misuse of Drugs Act

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that drug-related harm is significant and increasing in Aotearoa New Zealand, driven mainly by alcohol, methamphetamine, and emerging cocaine use. Dependence on alcohol or other drugs affects a person’s physical and mental health, relationships, employment, and personal finances. It can also affect the family and friends of people who use drugs and the victims of drug-related or drug-funded crime.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ramp up funding for harm reduction and addiction support for people who reduce or stop their drug intake, including through kaupapa Māori, rainbow, youth and harm reduction programmes. This would include funding innovative approaches to working with groups where smoking rates are disproportionately high, such as Tagata Moana and Māori. It would provide age-appropriate education about substance use disorders in schools and ensure harm reduction information is easily accessible for everyone.

policies.statement: Increase funding for harm reduction from drugs and addiction support services

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that all New Zealanders need to live with dignity and safety. Rainbow New Zealanders, in particular, need access to public services and healthcare that meet their needs.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would work with rainbow communities and organisations to develop strategies for wellbeing, especially for access to health care. Māori and Pasifika services specifically would also be included. Rainbow community organisations would receive dedicated resources for their work and be involved in developing and delivering services.

policies.statement: Increase resourcing for rainbow community organisations

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that all New Zealanders need to be able to live with dignity and safety. Rainbow New Zealanders in particular need access to public services and healthcare that serve their needs. This includes healthcare that supports their gender identity and removing barriers, such as surgery for intersex people and the ban on puberty blockers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would provide timely, non-discriminatory access to gender-affirming healthcare, such as hormones and surgery. These treatments would be given more resources in the health system, and the focus would be on informed consent and self-determination. The ban on puberty blockers would be revoked.

policies.statement: Ensure rainbow communities can access gender-affirming healthcare

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that all New Zealanders need to be able to live with dignity and safety. Rainbow New Zealanders in particular need their identities to be recognised and protected, as recommended by the Law Commission’s Ia Tangata report. Protecting human rights means being protected from non-consensual surgeries, and that rainbow migrants have their identities recognised and protected.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would amend the Human Rights Act to clarify that all forms of sexual orientation, gender identity and variations in sex characteristics, are prohibited grounds of discrimination and adopt the recommendations of the Ia Tangata report. Non-consensual and medically unnecessary surgeries for intersex people would be prohibited. Migrants, asylum seekers and refugees with rainbow identities would be able to access legal services, have their gender and partners legally recognised, and reunite with their families.

policies.statement: Promote the human rights of takatāpui, intersex and rainbow people against discrimination

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that all our activities should aim to eliminate waste, circulate resources and regenerate nature. It believes in transitioning to a zero-waste economy, where single-use plastics are largely eliminated and a circular product stewardship system, from design to disposal, is in place across the economy.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would work towards phasing out landfills and resource zero-waste strategies and legislation. It would develop and resource a national resource recovery network. It would promote moderate consumption and ban most single-use plastics. It would lead international efforts to clean up waste from the Pacific Ocean.

citations.title: 'Waste and Hazardous substances policy', undated (accessed 17 September 2026)
'Waste and Hazardous Substances Policy' (PDF), undated (accessed 17 December 2025)

policies.statement: Form a strategy for a zero-waste economy

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ needs to transition to a zero-waste economy, where single use plastics are largely eliminated, wasteful consumption is ended, and a circular product stewardship is in place across the economy.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require all products using plastics and rare earth metals to be readily recycled. Most single-use plastic products and non-recyclable and non-home-compostable packaging would be banned, with necessary exceptions.

citations.title: 'Waste and Hazardous substances policy', undated (accessed 17 September 2026)
'Waste and Hazardous Substances Policy' (PDF), undated (accessed 17 December 2025)

policies.statement: Ban single-use plastics and require plastics or rare earth materials to be recycled

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone is entitled to secure and meaningful work in innovative, environmentally sustainable, and socially responsible workplaces. That includes fair pay, freedom from discrimination and an equitable relationship between employers, union and workers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure pay equity, such as requiring pay transparency and pay-parity management, and ensure everyone including marginalised groups get the training and information they need to have equitable employment opportunities. It would support people whose work has been affected by climate change, and progress towards a shorter standard working week It would ensure time in lieu or overtime is provided for work out of contracted hours.

policies.statement: Support better working conditions including pay equity rules

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone is entitled to secure and meaningful work in innovative, environmentally sustainable, and socially responsible workplaces. That includes fair pay, freedom from discrimination and an equitable relationship between employers, unions, and workers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would make union membership an opt-out option when people start a new job. Newly hired employees would be default, be members unless they wish not to be.

policies.statement: Support default union membership for new workers

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that public services are investments in our shared future. Capable public servants need a strong grasp of Māori language, culture, and Te Tiriti o Waitangi as NZ's founding document in order to deliver services effectively.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would improve training in Te Tiriti and te reo Māori for all public servants, so that results across agencies are more consistent.

policies.statement: Improve training in te reo Māori and Te Tiriti o Waitangi for all public servants

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that independent commissions with expertise, like the Climate Change Commission, Human Rights Commission and Children's Commission play an important role. Public services ensure that all New Zealanders can thrive, and these commissions are part of how issues are monitored.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would restore the "monitoring" function of the Children's Commissioner, in addition to the advocacy function. It would also support the importance of independent commissions in the government more broadly.

policies.statement: Restore the monitoring role of the Children's Commissioner

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that public services need to be owned by the public, and the government's fiscal management needs to be future focused, not just based on short cycles. Public services should be funded to do their job properly and remain in public ownership, and the government's fiscal management should promote wellbeing, health, resilience and productivity.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reform the public finance system to create an approach that supports resilience, wellbeing, and productivity. It would fund public services adequately and ensure that public services and state owned enterprises continue to be owned by the government.

policies.statement: Reform the public finance system to focus on resilience, productivity and wellbeing

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone must be able to live free from violence and abuse. Aotearoa has among the highest rates of intimate partner violence, sexual violence and child abuse, and this is disproportionately harmful to people in vulnerable professions and families.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would invest in services to help victims and increase awareness of the drivers of violence and of restorative practices. It would fund a national strategy to eliminate family and sexual violence (Te Aorerekura) and amend the Crimes Act to criminalise coercive control. It would also amend the definition of consent. and restore relationship and sexuality teaching guidelines in all schools. Funding would be lifted for mental health support for victims and others in the justice system.

policies.statement: Support measures to reduce violence

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ has enough to invest in services for everyone, and community organisations, marae, iwi and hapū fulfil important roles in responding to the needs of their communities. These organisations should receive more money to meet the needs of their communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund Māori organisations, marae, iwi and hapū for community and environmental work. It would also provide secure and flexible funding arrangements to the community sector to recognise the importance of its work and ensuring community work and remain independent.

policies.statement: Fund community organisations and marae to fulfil the needs of their communities and regions

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that underinvestment has hurt public services and damaged their ability to fulfil their responsibilities to the public, leaving services stretched. Staff members in any part of the public sector should have access to the same pay and career progression to make things equal, improve retention and develop capacity and skills. The public service should also lead the way in providing flexible employment options for disabled people.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure all public servants can access career progression, pay, community secondment opportunities and training in all sectors. It would provide resources and training to meet disabled employees access needs and counter ableism.

policies.statement: Standardise pay and other support across the public sector

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that increasing numbers of New Zealanders are moving or living overseas, and the government represents these people too. New Zealanders living overseas deserve to connect to Aotearoa, and tangata whenua should always be able to return to their turangawaewae by being New Zealand citizens, regardless of where they were born.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would allow all people with Māori whakapapa to become New Zealand citizens, even if they have been born in another country.

policies.statement: Allow people with Māori whakapapa to become New Zealand citizens no matter where they are born

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that increasing numbers of New Zealanders are moving or living overseas, and the government represents these people too. New Zealanders overseas are still invested in the future of the country and should be able to vote. If they return to New Zealand and contribute here again, they should be able to receive superannuation.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would extend the time New Zealanders can live overseas and retain voting eligibility. Currently, overseas-based New Zealanders must have lived in NZ continuously for 12 months at some point in their life and been in NZ at some point in the last three years.

policies.statement: Extend the time New Zealanders can live overseas and retain voting eligibility

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that overseas New Zealanders deserve to remain connected to NZ, and have a interest in the future of the country. Nearly 15 percent of New Zealanders live in other countries. The government should take a compassionate approach to New Zealanders who have lived or are living overseas.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would restore the 10-year period of being based in NZ for superannuation eligibility.

policies.statement: Return to a 10-year period based in New Zealand for superannuation eligibility

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that overseas New Zealanders deserve to remain connected to NZ, and have an interest in the future of the country. Nearly 15% of New Zealanders live in other countries and many have moved overseas recently. The government should take a compassionate approach to New Zealanders who have lived or are living overseas. People with student loans should not face harsh consequences or border arrests.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reduce student loan interest rates for New Zealanders in other countries. It would cease the practice or arresting people at the NZ border for not repaying their student loans and extend the repayment holiday for people living overseas.

policies.statement: Make it easier for people based in other countries to repay student loans

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that overseas New Zealanders deserve to remain connected to NZ, and have a interest in the future of the country. Nearly 15% of New Zealanders live in other countries. The government should take a compassionate approach to New Zealanders who have lived or are living overseas. These people, and visitors from other countries to New Zealand, should be able to access public services like healthcare wherever they are.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would seek further reciprocal arrangements with other countries where New Zealanders might live. These would include access to public healthcare, welfare support or benefits and visa waivers. In return, the citizens of those countries would be offered the same services in New Zealand. Existing arrangements, as already exist in some form with the UK and Australia, could be widened to include temporary visitors as well as people working.

policies.statement: Pursue reciprocal healthcare, welfare and visa-waiver arrangements with other countries

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says our rail system has fallen into disarray, and our spread-out communities are poorly served by bus networks. Young people, non-car owners, families and minority groups all benefit from better transport options, as does the environment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would extend the Community Connect programme to provide free fares for young people, disabled and community service card holders. It would also work towards more bike lanes, and e-bike sharing.

policies.statement: Introduce free public transport fares for young people, the disabled and CSC card holders

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our rail system has fallen into disarray, and our communities are poorly served by our bus networks, particularly on the outskirts of towns. Young people, non-car owners, families and minority groups all benefit from better transport options, as does the environment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would build mass rapid transit in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and invest in a national passenger and freight rapid rail system to connect major cities and regions better. It would also fund affordable inter-regional and rural bus services and beef up bus lanes in cities.

policies.statement: Build mass rapid transit in three major cities and invest in better rail and bus links

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ's public transport system has left many people with no option but to rely on cars to get around, adding to congestion and making people vulnerable to oil price shocks. Young people, non-car owners, families and minority groups particularly benefit from better transport options, as does the environment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would phase out the importation of fossil-fuel vehicles, and build more electric vehicle charging stations, promote EV charging stations, car-sharing and introduce incentives for EV uptake.

policies.statement: Phase out fossil-fuel vehicle imports and incentivise electric vehicles

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that two supermarket companies control what almost everyone in New Zealand eats and are taking about $1m a day in profit. This party says that in a cost of living crisis, there should be greater competition in the grocery sector so everyone can afford healthy and nutritious food.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would break up the supermarket duopoly by requiring at least 120 stores and distribution centre capacity to be sold into public ownership. These would be folded into KiwiMart, a publicly owned supermarket chain with a mandate to prioritise affordability. It would also ban price gouging through legislation and introduce a pricing accuracy system which would compensate shoppers if overcharged. 
This is part of a wider policy which would establish a National Food Strategy, a beefed up Commerce Commission, more money for community-led food security and food grants, and a restored and expanded school lunch programme.  The cost of setting up KiwiMart would be $2.8bn.

citations.title: 'Greens launch plan to break up the supermarket duopoly and bring down the price of food', 6 September 2026 (accessed 18 September 2026)
'Affordable food for all of us' (PDF), undated (accessed 22 September 2026)

policies.statement: Break up the supermarket duopoly and use part of it to create a government-owned supermarket

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the current government has cut climate funding to the Pacific, threatening prosperity and damaging relationships with these neighbouring countries. With the risk of climate change, Pacific countries should be supported to adapt and reduce emissions. Projects should be lead by the Pacific, and the marine environment in this crucial part of the world should be taken care of too.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would restore climate funding to the Pacific to previous levels, and increase funding where needed. Pasifika people would also be resourced to lead climate action in NZ.
