This party would also support Pacific countries with ocean protection, enforcing protected areas under the High Seas Treaty and increasing funding for the South Pacific Regional Environment Programme.

policies.statement: Increase climate aid funding to the Pacific

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that our education system should be lifelong and accessible to everyone. But currently students struggle to pay for and stay in tertiary education - including vocational and community adult education - and providers are struggling to provide courses and attract and retain talent..

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would provide fees-free tertiary education, reduce student loan repayments, and work towards a write-off of student loan debt. It would also introduce a universal student allowance for tertiary students to cover their needs, and training allowances for those doing compulsory work placements.

policies.statement: Introduce fees-free tertiary education, universal student allowances and paid placements

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that Pacific peoples are an important part of building NZ's sustainable and flourishing future. Pacific communities are some of the youngest and fastest-growing in NZ. However, it can be hard for their family from Pacific Island countries to visit NZ, and workers under the RSE (Recognised Seasonal Employer) scheme can be mistreated.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would extend visa-free travel to NZ for citizens of Pacific countries. It would also replace the current RSE scheme with an alternative that guarantees housing and fair wages, and create an open work system where it is easier for these workers to change employers if they are not being treated well. Workers under the new scheme would have a clearer path to NZ residency.

policies.statement: Increase visa-free travel and work visa set-ups for Pasifika visitors and workers in NZ

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that education should be lifelong and accessible to all. In reality, tertiary education is cost-prohibitive to many, and the institutions themselves struggle with funding to keep courses open and attract and retain good teachers and researchers. Polytechnics are underfunded and don't always meet community needs and  more apprenticeship programmes are needed.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would ensure polytechnics have adequate funding and strong local control to meet workforce and community needs, and protect staff and courses. 
Tertiary organisations would receive a funding formula that prioritises teaching, pastoral care, and research, with a focus on collaboration rather than competition between providers. 
Apprenticeship programmes would be expanded and all tertiary education would be fees-free.

policies.statement: Ensure proper resourcing for tertiary education providers

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ deserves a tertiary education system that is affordable, equitable and which gives students the support they need to succeed.  This system would recognise te Tiriti and deliver equitable outcomes for tauira Māori (Māori students).

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would expand the Māori and Pasifika Trades Training programme and ensure all tertiary institutes uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi and deliver equitable outcomes for tauira Māori (Māori students). It would fully resource Whare Wānanga to increase opportunities for kaupapa Māori education.

citations.title: 'National moves the goalposts on jobs', 8 October 2026 (accessed 08 October 2026)

policies.statement: Expand the Māori and Pasifika Trades Training Programme and make tertiary education more equitable for Māori students

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that te Tiriti must be upheld as the fundamental document that the Treaty of Waitangi Act is based on. In its view, successive governments have consistently breached Te Tiriti, eroding the true partnership that was intended. Te Tiriti o Waitangi references have recently been weakened or stripped out of 19 acts of Parliament. And in government decision-making, iwi and hapū are often treated as advisors, rather than the partners which they are meant to be.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would amend the Treaty of Waitangi Act so Te Tiriti is the authoritative text. It would implement genuine Te Tiriti decision-making models across government, and ensure iwi and hapu are resourced to participate as partners.
It would increase resourcing for the Waitangi Tribunal and give it the power to make binding recommendations for the return of Crown and private land. 
It would facilitate the return of whenua outside of Treaty Settlements that was wrongfully alienated from tangata whenua, including a possible right-of-first-refusal process at point of sale. It would also reform the Treaty Settlements process to enable fair negotiations and just reparations without cessation of sovereignty.

policies.statement: Uphold te Tiriti in the Treaty of Waitangi Act and across government decision-making

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that small businesses are facing an economy that is stacked against them. Liquidations are the highest in almost 15 years and a lack of supermarket competition is squeezing shoppers and local suppliers. International corporates are flourishing while factories close and local businesses struggle. This party will work for an even playing field for local businesses and support sustainable low-carbon industries.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would encourage consumer to support local by revitalising ‘Buy Kiwi Made’ and expanding country of origin labelling; commit government departments to buying more NZ goods and services; reform competition laws to create a fairer playing field for small businesses and consumers. It would foster sustainable, low carbon jobs in the ICT sector, particularly smaller firms. And it would invest in community-led regional development with a focus on sustainable building, regenerative agriculture, low-carbon infrastructure and iwi/hapū led economic activity.

policies.statement: Support NZ made products, small business and sustainable industries

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that small businesses are faced with a challenging landscape including a 15-year high in liquidations and a lack of supermarket competition which is squeezing local suppliers. Small businesses need an even playing field against international corporates where the profits go offshore.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reform competition laws to create a fairer playing field for small businesses and consumers. It would also increase the resources and powers of regulatory agencies investigating anti-competitive behaviour.

policies.statement: Better resource the agencies fighting anti-competitive practices

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that seniors have cared for us and many continue to do so during retirement. They should feel valued, connected and able to live with dignity. Seniors should have warm, accessible homes, and the community spaces and marae-based centres that support them should they need assistance. The says that, additionally, there should also be more support for the conditions and pay of aged care workers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would launch a long‑term seniors strategy that addresses kaumātua wellbeing, elder abuse, equitable incomes, and the creation of a state‑owned, not‑for‑profit retirement village system. It would boost funding for senior community spaces and activities, expand housing options such as papakāinga and address social housing waitlists for kaumātua. It would support warm, accessible, smaller home designs and back fair pay and conditions for aged care workers.

policies.statement: Create a state-owned retirement village system and more support for seniors

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that democratic engagement in local government is low, especially at turnout for local elections. Local government should have a mandate from communities and local elections should be consistent across the country, rather than being run by different private companies.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would transfer responsibility of local elections to the Electoral Commission. Sixteen year olds would be allowed to vote in local elections and all councils would use a Single Transferable Vote (STV) system. To enhance democracy and community input, councils could use tools like citizens assemblies to make decisions, especially regarding reorganisation of council bodies.

policies.statement: Transfer responsibility for local elections to the Electoral Commission

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that tino rangatiratanga is often sidelined in council decision making. Local government shapes a lot of people's everyday life, and community wellbeing should be a priority.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reinforce the role of local government to give effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and formally establish local councils as Te Tiriti partners. Councils would be allowed to reinstate Māori wards. Councils should also consider multiple sphere through the "four wellbeings" (social, economic, environmental and cultural) and take responsibility for more areas from central government, with appropriate resourcing.

policies.statement: Ensure that fulfilling Te Tiriti and wellbeing goals is a core responsibility of local government

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that councils have been loaded with new responsibilities like emergency management and tourist influxes, but not given enough money to carry out these responsibilities. To carry out their role in communities, councils should not have limits on rates set by central government. Instead they need appropriate resourcing from a range of tools.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reject the proposed rates cap where councils could only increase rates between 2 and 4 percent annually. Councils could set rates as they chose. Councils would also be allowed to use bed levies, congestion charging and charge GST on rates and other growth.

policies.statement: Reject the proposed rates cap and allow councils to use more funding tools

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that people experiencing mental distress deserve access to care, no matter where they are. Social factors like the climate crisis, poverty and unemployment exacerbate the mental health crisis in NZ. Mental health services should be well funded and integrated into the public health system, not fragmented and requiring people to turn to private services which also have long waiting lists. Harmful practices, like seclusion, should be phased out so that care does not cause further harm

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would extend free mental health care to all communities, with more funding for community-specific mental health care. This includes youth services like Piki, Mana Ake and Youth One Stop Shops throughout Aotearoa. It also includes Asian Family Services and dedicated support for postnatal mental health. Mental health facilities would be further resourced so that the practice of seclusion could be phased out, replaced by community care models. Specific kaupapa Māori mental health and addiction programmes, including programmes focused on youth, would be funded as well.

policies.statement: Expand free mental health services to all communities

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that all people in distress should be able to access support, especially as social factors like poverty, unemployment and climate change worsen mental health outcomes. Caring for those in distress and ensuring mental health workers are funded and resourced to avoid burnout will lead to better outcomes.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would implement all the recommendations in Every Life Matters – He Tapu te Oranga o ia Tangata Suicide Prevention Strategy. It would also commit to further actions identified as part of a kaupapa Māori suicide prevention strategy, especially those aimed at reducing suicide among people younger than 24.

policies.statement: Implement suicide prevention recommendations, especially focused on youth

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone deserves to access quality mental health care in the community where they live. Services should be culturally relevant and focused on the area of greatest need. With demand high and mental health workers burned out, making referral to secondary services clear, fast and consistent will lead to good outcomes.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would link primary health and secondary mental health services with clear referral pathways in every health region. The focus would be on areas that have disproportionate need.

policies.statement: Connect primary and secondary mental health care with clear referral pathways

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that a warm safe home should be a basic right, but much of NZ's housing is a source of misery and expense, while people who can afford to own their homes get richer. Housing should be affordable and healthy.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase the stringency of the current Healthy Homes Standards for rental housing. It would also introduce a "Rental Warrant of Fitness" to certify that a house was appropriate to rent out, which would be independently certified.

policies.statement: Create an independently enforced Rental Warrant of Fitness

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that housing should be a basic right, not a "get rich quick" scheme only for those who can afford it. Building affordable, sustainable homes in the places where people want to live will focus on housing for homes, rather than housing as an investment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase public housing stock by building tens of thousands of new homes. It would fund papakāinga to be built on Māori land. People in need of emergency housing would be guaranteed "same-day" placement, and concepts like "housing first" and supported housing would be used for those in most need to support them to build a life in a stable home.

policies.statement: Increase public housing supply and housing support

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that housing should be a basic right, not an investment that a lucky few can get rich from. Renting should be fixed so that healthy homes in places where people want to live are affordable.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would limit annual rent increases to no more than 2 percent per year. The amount charged in rent for a new tenancy would be linked to what previous tenancies paid, so that there is not a jump in price between tenants.

policies.statement: Limit annual rent increases to 2 percent

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that AI data centres can currently be consented by councils with no community input. Overseas, data centres have had adverse effects on local water supplies and are high energy users, driving up power prices. The Datagrid data centre in Southland is expected to use 6 per cent of the country's electricity supply. This party says there needs to be more transparency and a chance for regulation to be developed.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would call for a one-year moratorium on new AI data centres while proper rules are put in place to ensure there are benefits and don't unduly strain our resources. Solutions could include forcing centres to build their own energy or use closed loop water cooling systems, but currently there are no requirements for these under NZ rules.

citations.title: 'Call for a One Year Pause on Consenting New AI Data Centres', 26 July 2026 (accessed 18 August 2026)

policies.statement: Implement a one-year pause on AI data centers

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that a home is a place to build a life with loved ones. Building houses in existing urban areas will prevent cities from encroaching into rural areas, and mean homes are more sustainable for the next generation.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require councils to collaborate with communities, including mana whenua on decisions about new housing. Housing should be in mixed-use areas with shops and housing, within existing urban areas, and prioritise being able to walk around easily.

policies.statement: Encourage mixed-use areas and walkability in new housing developments

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ produces enough food to feed 40 million people, but somehow food prices are too high for many. Dismantling the supermarket duopoly alone is not enough to deliver food security, and demand for community solutions like food banks is immense. This party would offer more support to those building alternative models for food security, processing and distribution.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would double the cap on food grants at the cost of $94-$100m annually. It would lift funding for regional food distribution hubs and community food providers from up to $8m to $25m a year and set up a $150m a year Fair Food Fund for community-led food security, such as food rescue programmes, marae and social supermarkets.

citations.title: 'Greens launch plan to break up the supermarket duopoly and bring down the price of food', 6 September 2026 (accessed 22 September 2026)
'Affordable food for all of us' (PDF), undated (accessed 22 September 2026)

policies.statement: Increase funding for food grants, food banks and other food security programmes

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that early childhood education costs are a stress and barrier for many families, and that education should be a public good. This party says the competitive market in education has reduced trust, creativity and maintained exclusion.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would first cap charges at $10 per day per child, on top of the 20 hour per week entitlement that is currently funded. This party would raise the funded entitlement to 35 hours a week by 2029.

citations.title: 'Green Budget: Early Childhood Education for Everyone ', 14 May 2025 (accessed 22 September 2026)

policies.statement: Make early childhood education free

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that children learn better when they are well-fed and every child deserves healthy, delicious and locally prepared food.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would restore Ka Ora, Ka Ako, the healthy school lunch programme, so lunches are provided by schools and local providers. Expand the school lunch programme to 400 more schools, providing lunches to 150,000 more schoolchildren. It would permanently fund the school lunch programme.

citations.title: 'Affordable food for all of us' (PDF), undated (accessed 22 September 2026)
'Green Party announces plan for free and nutritious school lunches', 20 August 2026 (accessed 20 September 2026)

policies.statement: Expand the school lunch program

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that a healthy environment is important for healthy communities. It says mining projects approved by the fast-track act are destructive to wild environments.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would repeal the Fast-track approvals act and revoke consents for new coal, gold or seabed mining projects.

policies.statement: Repeal the Fast-track Approvals Act

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that restoration and protection of the environment is important for the future and that a strong ministry is important for this.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would restore the Ministry for the Environment, and increase resources for the Environmental Protection Authority to identify risks to the environment and to support compliance, monitoring and enforcement. It would also re-establish resources for the Community Environment Fund.

policies.statement: Restore the Ministry for the Environment

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the current government's reforms to curriculums and assessments are rushed and ideological. This party believes education should foster curiosity, creativity and confidence, be grounded in Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and decisions should centre educators voices and expertise. This party says decisions are driven by standardisation and ranking reduces trust and creativity and re-enforces exclusion in education.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would reset the current reforms and revert to the original direction of Te Mātaiaho, the New Zealand curriculum, and ensure reforms to qualifications follows reforms to the curriculum.

policies.statement: Reset reforms to the curriculum and NCEA

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that education is vital for social cohesion and democracy and should be planned and funded to deliver this.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support the workforce to get fair wages and reach staffing levels that support quality teaching, and co-develop a long-term workforce plan with the sector.

policies.statement: Develop a long-term plan to support the teaching workforce

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that democracy should work for everyone, not just the wealthy. Capping donations and increasing the transparency around lobbying mean big money and professional lobbying can have less influence over politics.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would bring in a package of reforms, including a public register for lobbying so meetings with politicians are on the record. Former ministers would have to wait two years before they can be employed by a lobbying group. A new bill would cap party donations at $30,000 per individuals, and companies will not be able to donate. Donors above $1000 would have to be named.

citations.title: 'Greens announce plans to get big money and influence out of politics', 22 September 2026 (accessed 22 September 2026)

policies.statement: Regulate lobbying and party donations

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that people with disabilities and diverse learners should be fully supported to learn, belong and thrive.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would expand the criteria for access to learning support and establish a single agency for specialist supports for learners with health and disability needs. It would implement all actions in the Ministry for Educations 'Framework for Action: A Quality Education for All' strategy.

policies.statement: Expand access to learning support

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that education should be grounded in Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and Māori voices and communities should be central to decision making. It believes education should honour tino rangatiratanga and embrace te reo Māori and mātauranga Māori.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would work towards a Māori Education Authority which governs and funds all Māori medium and Kaupapa Māori education. This party would support Māori communities to provide an education system that is driven by whānau needs and makes whakapapa-based decisions.

policies.statement: Work towards creating a Māori Education Authority

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that shared-decision making between the Government and tangata whenua is important to uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and that this has been taken out of environmental laws.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would secure the role of Te Tiriti in the resource management system and affirm the role of tangata whenua as shared decision-makers and kaitiaki (guardians). The party will also implement strong evidence-based limits for ecosystem health.

citations.title: 'Greens commit to undoing attacks on conservation and environment laws', 19 September 2026 (accessed 22 September 2026)

policies.statement: Uphold Te Tiriti o Waitangi in the new resource management system

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that women deserve to be paid fairly and the same as men for equal work. This party says changes made by the Government to pay equity shifted the goal posts for pay equity claims.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would undo the current Government's changes to pay equity and resume pay equity claims, pay transparency measures and pay gap reporting.

policies.statement: Reverse changes to pay equity and fair pay agreements

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that women face disparities in healthcare, especially for pelvic pain conditions and endometriosis.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would work towards diagnosing and treating endometriosis faster. It would develop formal clinical guidelines for diagnosing and treating endometriosis, and fund specialist clinics for endometriosis across NZ.

policies.statement: Improve endometriosis treatment

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that single mothers are vulnerable to hardship and need more support.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund a one-stop-shop service for new parents, providing pā harakeke wrap-around suppport for whānau during pregnancy, after birth, in early childhood, and throughout parenthood.  This is in addition to its policy to extent paid parental leave.

policies.statement: Create wrap-around services for new parents

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that gender-based violence is increasing, and front-line organisations should be resourced to end family and and sexual violence in NZ.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would will resource kaupapa Māori and community-led solutions to family and sexual violence. These solutions would be developed by groups that are disproportionately impacted by family and sexual violence, including women, Pasifika, rainbow and disabled communities.

policies.statement: Support kaupapa Māori and community based solutions to family and sexual violence

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that gender-based violence is increasing and women and gender minorities should be safe, respected and valued.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would amend the Crimes Act to amend the definition of consent and affirm that consent must be free and voluntary, and can be withdrawn at any time.

policies.statement: Amend the definition of consent to be free and voluntary

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that gender-based violence is increasing and women and gender minorities should be safe, respected and valued.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would amend the Crimes Act to criminalise coercive control.

policies.statement: Criminalise coercive control

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that women and families deserve to be safe and supported. Women deserve to get paid for their work, and compensated for time at home carrying out the essential work of caregiving.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase paid parental leave to 15 months for the primary caregiver, and have additional ring-fenced leave for partners. This party would also increase payments.

policies.statement: Extend paid parental leave to 15 months

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that towns and cities need help to keep their centres vibrant. Empty shops are apparent on most main streets because of high rents set when the market was stronger. Many commercial leases don't allow for a rent review below the level set.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would ensure market rent reviews can lower rents as well as raise them. This will apply to both new and existing leases for businesses with a turnover of under $30m. 
It would also give councils the power to auction leases on shops that have been empty for more than a year, and a low-cost tribunal will be established for commercial lease disputes.

citations.title: 'Greens announce plan for city centre vibrancy ', 19 September 2026 (accessed 22 September 2026)

policies.statement: Fill empty stores by changing retail lease rules and addressing vacant buildings

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the government's push for automated decision erroneously left tens of thousands of financially vulnerable people without funds.  Similar issues overseas have proven why decisions on who receives financial support should not be left to algorithms.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would not use AI and automated decision making for welfare payment decisions such as cancelling, suspending, or reducing welfare payments, or imposing benefit sanctions.

citations.title: 'Green Party pledge to remove AI from welfare payment decisions', 11 September 2026 (accessed 16 September 2026)

policies.statement: Refuse to use AI for decisions on welfare payments

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that NZ should be an independent voice against global atrocities, authoritarians, and imperialist ambitions. This party says most United Nations member states have already recognised Palestinian statehood.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would recognise Palestine as a state and pass a bill drafted by this party to sanction Israel.

citations.title: ' Govt’s empty words do nothing to stop genocide in Gaza ', 11 August 2025 (accessed 23 September 2026)

policies.statement: Recognise Palestine as a state and sanction Israel

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that war and authoritarianism is rising globally, and NZ should be an independent voice for peace, freedom, democracy, and should speak out against nuclear weapons and American militarism. This party says foreign policy should challenge imperialism that creates chaos and hardship, and should always support countries facing conflicts and human rights abuses.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would withdraw NZ from the Five Eyes security alliance and decline to participate in AUKUS, as part of efforts to step away from military and security frameworks with the United States. This party would rewrite NZ's foreign policy to stand against human rights abuses and focus on upholding peace and justice, and would have the Defence Force focus on climate change, humanitarian responses and environmental monitoring.

policies.statement: Rewrite foreign policy to oppose imperialism

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that NZ should work with Pacific neighbours to create a greener, safer, and more just world. This party says NZ should be a world leader on issues of climate action, protection of nature and indigenous and human rights, and should work to uphold the international rule of law and collective obligations towards issues like climate change.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support Pacific sovereignty, independence, and oppose militarisation in the Pacific. This party would also support decolonisation and democracy movements globally, including those of indigenous peoples in Asia-Pacific region and work to urgently progress climate change initiatives through international institutions. It would support calls for West Papua to be independent of Indonesia, and for French-ruled Polynesian islands to be independent and call for an indigenous-led human rights investigation and a visit from the UN's Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous People.

policies.statement: Support sovereignty and independence in the Asia-Pacific

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that NZ should have an independent approach to foreign affairs and trade that focuses on climate action, nature protection, indigenous and human rights.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would implement a suite of measures including increased democratic scrutiny of trade agreements, and enforceable recognition of Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations, workers’ rights, human rights and climate commitments in trade agreements.

policies.statement: Increase democratic scrutiny of trade agreements

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that harmful drug use must be treated first as a health issue, rather than a criminal justice issue. While there can be adverse consequences from drug use, not all drug use is abusive or problematic, and evidence indicates making substance use illegal makes it harder for people to seek help. In terms of drugs, cannabis causes far less harm than alcohol, methamphetamine, cocaine, or tobacco.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would regulate cannabis for legal personal use, with a legal age limit. Previous criminal convictions for these offences are removed from all records. Cultivation for personal use would generally be no longer illegal, and an evidence-based approach would be taken on which regulatory model best minimises harm. This includes improving drug-driving laws and providing education on the harmful effects of heavy or prolonged cannabis use.
Medicinal cannabis would be accessible and affordable for patients.

policies.statement: Decriminalise cannabis for personal use

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone should have reliable access to public healthcare, including during and after civil emergencies. This party says hospitals and GP clinics are stretched and over-capacity, and suffering from under-investment from successive Governments. It says private provider costs in healthcare are preventing people from seeking help early, causing health issues to escalate.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would work towards free public primary healthcare and dental care, that can be accessed by everyone. They would increase focus on prevention and early screening, early diagnosis and treatment of non-communicable diseases, such as kidney disease, cancers, diabetes, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. This party would fund the creation of mobile clinics for health care, mental health, diagnostic services and dental vans, for rural communities and during and after civil emergencies, including by-Māori, for-Māori community clinics. This party would also increase funding for data and digital infrastructure and capability in the health sector. This party would also regulate providers of private infrastructure and hold them to high standards of privacy.

policies.statement: Increase free public health services

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that Hauora Māori and social service providers of healthcare are underfunded and restricted by contracts that are overly prescriptive. This party says Māori are underserved by the health system, and that progress to provide equitable healthcare has been undone. This party says kaupapa Māori health services should be supported to end health inequalities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would stop overly prescriptive Hauora service contracts. This party would simplify and improve funding arrangements for providers of health services for whānau, hapū iwi and hapori. They would commit to working with Iwi Māori partnership boards and Hauora Māori to do this.

policies.statement: Simplify funding for Hauora Māori providers

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that under-investment in health services has led to an understaffed hospital workforce and GP clinics that can't accept new enrollments. They say there are unsafe conditions for health workers and lengthy wait times. This party says everyone should be able to access timely healthcare from a supported workforce

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure all health workers have fair wages. They would fund pay parity for primary care and hauora providers. This party would set safe staffing levels, to improve worker wellbeing and quality of care.

policies.statement: Improve wages and staffing for health providers

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that Pharmac should invest in new health care devices and medicines so that treatment and quality of life for patients improves.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase sustained funding for Pharmac.

policies.statement: Increase funding for Pharmac

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that pharmacists should help treat common health issues and should be encouraged to give appropriate medical advice. This party says they should be compensated fairly to do so.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would Expand the Minor Health Conditions Service to help pharmacies treat common health issues, and update the Integrated community pharmacy services agreement to compensate pharmacists fairly.

policies.statement: Expand the conditions that pharmacies can treat

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that people coming to NZ for work should have fair and achievable pathways to residence. The party says that migrant workers are not disposable, yet they face exploitation, are denied basic rights and are unfairly targeted by immigration compliance officers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create new residency pathways for migrants who have settled in NZ long-term, including those whose visas have expired. This party would also allow migrant work visa holders to switch employers and would end the 12-month stand-down period requiring workers to leave the country between visas.

policies.statement: Support migrant workers to residency

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that says that migrants and refugees with health conditions or disabilities are discriminated against by the acceptable standards of health requirements.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would abolish the Acceptable Standards of Health requirements for visa applicants.

policies.statement: Abolish acceptable standards of health requirements for migrants and refugees

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that says that nobody should be unfairly separated from their families or communities. This party says people who flee war or persecution to seek asylum in New Zealand should be supported and treated with dignity.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would clear the backlog for refugee family reunification, including resourcing Immigration New Zealand to clear the backlog of tier 1 and 2 family reunification categories and process asylum claims quickly. This party would restore birthright citizenship, expand work rights for partners, remove income barriers to supporting a parent visa, and stop detention and electronic monitoring of asylum seekers.

policies.statement: Support families of migrants and refugees to get visas

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that people who fear for their life in their country, should be supported to seek a better life in NZ. They say people escaping war or persecution should be supported to rebuild their lives as part of our communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would progressively increase the refugee quota to 5,000 by 2029. This party would also increase funding for refugee resettlement programmes and create a new humanitarian visa for family of New Zealanders in conflict zones.

policies.statement: Increase the refugee quota

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says migrants and refugees should be supported to rebuild their lives in NZ.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would implement Māori aspirations for an immigration system based on Te Tiriti o Waitangi. It would develop resources and decision-making with iwi and hapū to strengthen traditional whanaungatanga connections. This party would also provide Te Tiriti education to new migrants and refugees.

policies.statement: Create an immigration system based on Te Tiriti o Waitangi

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone has a right to a liveable income that guarantees enough for food, safe housing and good quality of life. This party says the cost of living has got worse, and thousands of children go to bed hungry and families are struggling to pay rent or mortgages.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase benefits to liveable rates and individualise benefit entitlements. This party would also abolish benefit sanctions. The party would reform the Social Security Act to uphold dignity of people seeking support and ensure everyone has a secure income, and implement a high-trust working model at work and income. This party would also overhaul recoverable assistance grants, write off existing debt to MSD and ban attachment orders against beneficiaries.

policies.statement: Increase benefit payments and improve standards for beneficaries

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says a wealth tax is part of a fairer tax system, that can reduce income inequality and ensure everyone has enough to live. This party says multi-millionaires pay $9 in tax for every $100 they make, while teachers pay $22 in tax for every $100 they make. This party says a wealth tax makes super-rich New Zealanders pay a fair share.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would introduce a 2.5 percent tax on net wealth worth over $10m, with an exemption for the family home.

citations.title: 'Greens commit to tax the super-rich and large corporates fairly, cut income tax for 96% ', 21 June 2026 (accessed 23 September 2026)

policies.statement: Introduce a tax for net wealth over $10m

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that everyone deserves a livable income if they are unemployed, disabled, sick or a caregiver.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would extend ACC to cover income support and treatment for injuries, disability and illness, regardless of origin.

policies.statement: Expand ACC to cover income support and treatment

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that families are struggling to pay rent or mortgages, to feed their children, or to warm their homes, as the cost of living has worsened. This party says that families should be looked after at every stage of life.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase the working for families rate, reduce abatements and extend tax credits to families who are unemployed.

policies.statement: Strengthen working for families

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that rehabilitation is important to keep communities safe. It says current approaches to justice neglect rehabilitation, which causes more harm and hardship for communities.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would resource evidence-based rehabilitation for anyone convicted of an offence. Tikanga based and restorative justice solutions, like Te Pae Oranga, would be available to anyone to access. This party would also improve community re-integration support for offenders leaving the criminal justice system, and would increase the Steps to Freedom grant to cover at least 30 years of inflation.

policies.statement: Prioritise rehabilitation for convicted offenders

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the justice system should be safe, equitable and fair. This party aims to meet the basic needs of communities in order to prevent crime happening in the first place.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require body cameras for frontline police and strengthen the powers of the Independent Police Conduct Authority. The party would also deliver de-escalation and trauma training for police, and increase resourcing for Māori Wardens and Pacific Wardens.

policies.statement: Increase accountability in policing

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that says the justice system should be fair and equitable. This party says people should not be punished for being poor, and communities are safer when young people have access to food, healthcare, education and have a safe home environment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would end military-style academies for young people and raise the age of criminal responsibility. This party would also ban young people being detained alongside adults. This party would expand access to specialist youth courts, including the Rangatahi and Pasifika Courts, Alcohol and Other Drug Treatment Court, and New Beginnings Court, so young people across NZ could access them.

policies.statement: End military-style academies for young offenders

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the justice system should be fair and equitable, and communities should be supported to prevent crime happening in the first place.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would expand the district court initiative, Te Ao Marama, to all courts in New Zealand. This party would also extend legal aid and duty lawyers, better resource community law centres and make applications for protection and parenting orders free.

policies.statement: Improve accessibility to justice and legal assistance

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that laws restricting the decisions a judge can make about sentences have caused more harm and hardship. This party says bias and discrimination in the justice system should be addressed.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would help enable judicial discretion in sentencing. This includes ending mandatory minimum sentences, life sentences, preventive detention, limits on sentence discounts, three strikes and limits on when home detention can be imposed instead of imprisonment.

policies.statement: Reduce restrictions on the decisions judges can make

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that everyone deserves to live free from violence, harm and discrimination.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would extend hate speech laws to cover religion, gender, disability and rainbow communities. This party would implement this alongside other recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Terrorist Attack on Christchurch Mosques on 15 March 2019.

policies.statement: Extend hate speech laws

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that everyone deserves to live free from violence, harm and discrimination.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would implement all recommendations from the royal commission of inquiry, including passing hate speech laws, and continuing to oppose possession of military-style semi-automatic firearms.

policies.statement: Implement the recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Terrorist Attack on Christchurch Mosques on 15 March 2019

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that the Royal Commission of Inquiry into abuse in care was a harrowing account of how society and the Government failed, and must change. The party says survivors have called for all 138 recommendations to be implemented.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would implement all recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care, in consultation with people with lived experience of abuse in care.

citations.title: 'One year on from apology, Government still missing in action ', 12 November 2025 (accessed 23 September 2026)

policies.statement: Implement recommendations of Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that says it is important to take an evidenced, harm-reduction approach to alcohol and drugs.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would would phase out all alcohol advertising and sponsorship, including at sporting and cultural events, and use funding from the alcohol levy to establish a national harm-reduction campaign.

policies.statement: Ban alcohol advertising and sponsorship

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the 'war on drugs' approach from 50 years ago has increased harm and addictions, and diverts money away from public health services. This party supports an evidence-based approach that prioritises people's health.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would enable a licensing system for psychedelic treatment, and recognise taonga status of our native psylocibin (magic mushroom) species.

policies.statement: Enable licensing for psychedelic treatment

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that that funding for addiction services should be increased, and NZ should take a harm-reduction approach to alcohol and drugs. This party believes young people should be protected from nicotine by stronger regulations for retailers.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would phase out nicotine availability and fund culturally responsive vaping and smoking cessation services. This party would also implement stronger regulation and enforcement for nicotine retailers.

policies.statement: Reduce nicotine availability and fund culturally responsive services to quit smoking and vaping

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the previous pay equity law better protected care and support workers who look after disabled people, older people and some of the most vulnerable people in New Zealand every day. However, this law was changed in 2025, and since then, these workers have been undervalued. This party believes a carer's pay should reflect the skill and responsibility their jobs demand.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would restore the pay equity law to its pre-previous-government form. The party would also fund the settlement for the approximately 65,000 care and support workers whose claim was stopped after those changes were made to the law by passing legislation to settle the claim. The final settlement would be agreed through bargaining with the workers and their unions. This party estimates that this policy would cost $1.1 billion a year.

citations.title: 'Greens commit to pay equity for care workers', 1 October 2026 (accessed 02 October 2026)

policies.statement: Restore pay equity and negotiate a settlement for care workers

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealanders deserve a fast, convenient and affordable transport system. It believes that years of underinvestment in public transport have left our cities harder to get around without a car. However, it says our cities have the potential to be accessible, vibrant and connected for locals and visitors. This will make it easier and more affordable for people to get where they need to go using cleaner modes of transport, also helping to cut greenhouse gas emissions.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would make bus and train fares free for children, teenagers, students, apprentices, Community Service Card holders, and Total Mobility Users, and cap bus and train fares at $2 for adults.

citations.title: 'Green Party launches the transport plan to combat fossil fuel crisis', 4 October 2026 (accessed 05 October 2026)

policies.statement: Make public transport free for children and other specified people and cap fares at $2 for adults

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the fuel crisis is costing ordinary people every time they travel. We need transport alternatives that are more affordable, fast, frequent, and reliable. It says communities are currently designed to prioritise working best for cars, when they should be designed to work best for people.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund up to 150 new regional bus services to supplement existing services, extend the Te Huia train to Tauranga with track and tunnel improvements and pilot an overnight passenger train service between Wellington and Auckland. It would also bring back the Southerner train connection between Christchurch and Dunedin.

citations.title: 'Green Party launches the transport plan to combat fossil fuel crisis', 4 October 2026 (accessed 05 October 2026)
'Fast, frequent, affordable public transport for all of us', undated (accessed 05 October 2026)

policies.statement: Create improved public transport services between regions

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that New Zealanders spend too much time and money sitting in traffic, filling up the car, and waiting for trains and buses. This party says there needs to be more affordable and accessible alternatives to driving a car.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would deliver immediate improvements to bus routes along the planned Mass Rapid Transit routes in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and plan and deliver light rail or bus rapid transit in line with the Infrastructure Commission’s preferred option. The party would also fund Wellington’s critical rail renewal work needed to fix broken-down track assets and infrastructure. It would lastly work with Auckland Transport to fund and deliver level crossing removals to allow for more frequent trains, fewer delays, and better safety outcomes.

citations.title: 'Green Party launches the transport plan to combat fossil fuel crisis', 4 October 2026 (accessed 05 October 2026)
'Fast, frequent, affordable public transport for all of us', undated (accessed 05 October 2026)

policies.statement: Improve public transport within cities

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that regions are often left behind when it comes to public transport infrastructure upgrades, with the focus on major cities. It says that communities living in smaller towns also deserve the opportunity to access affordable and accessible public transport.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would fund the planned bus improvements in smaller cities and towns in the Waikato, Bay of Plenty, Taranaki, Horowhenua, and Otago. It would also work to revitalise town and city centres and increase safe walking and biking infrastructure.

citations.title: 'Green Party launches the transport plan to combat fossil fuel crisis', 4 October 2026 (accessed 05 October 2026)
'Fast, frequent, affordable public transport for all of us', undated (accessed 05 October 2026)

policies.statement: Fund public transport for the regions

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that everyone loves the Hauraki Gulf and we are supposed to protect and look after the things we love. This party wants to restore the marine ecosystem of the Gulf and ensure it is flourishing for generations to come.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would commit to the Hauraki Gulf Forum's goal of protecting 30% of the Gulf by 2030, as part of its wider plan to protect at least 30% of New Zealand's oceans by reforming marine protected area legislation. It would also remove the ring-net fishing exemption from the Gulf's high protection areas immediately, through a Bill released in early October. Iwi and hapū would be supported to lead ocean protection in the Gulf. As part of its wider conservation policy, the party would also enable the Gulf’s fisheries to be managed according to the health of the entire ecosystem by reviewing the Quota Management System.

citations.title: 'Greens announce plans to protect the Hauraki Gulf', 6 October 2026 (accessed 06 October 2026)

policies.statement: Protect 30% of the Hauraki Gulf by 2030

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that over the last 10 years, there have been almost 70 crashes and hundreds of near-misses at level crossings across Auckland. Removing them will allow for better safety outcomes, more frequent trains and fewer delays.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would work with the Auckland Council to identify the best options to fund and deliver level crossing removals.

citations.title: 'Greens Commit To Funding And Delivering Level Crossing Removals', 5 October 2026 (accessed 06 October 2026)

policies.statement: Fund and deliver level crossing removals in Auckland

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that youth unemployment is at nearly 15 per cent, roughly three times that of the wider working-age population, which is at an 11-year high. Yet there is so much work to be done in New Zealand. This party says it does not make sense, with nearly 100,000 young people not in employment, training or education. A long period without a job at the start of a working life also lowers a person’s wages for years afterwards.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would establish the Jobs for Young People pilot programme, based on the successful Jobs for Nature model, to support new jobs in businesses, councils, iwi, non-profits or the public sector. It would also scale up funding of the Mayor's Taskforce for Jobs for all 67 councils, connecting young people with local businesses, community organisations, iwi and hapū. Lastly, it would make sure there is a national workforce strategy plan for young people.

citations.title: 'Greens announce jobs guarantee for young people', 11 October 2026 (accessed 12 October 2026)

policies.statement: Guarantee every 16-to 24-year-old who has been out of work for six months a pathway into education, training, or a new job

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that artificial intelligence should support human judgement, not replace it. Decisions that affect people's rights, welfare, health, education, employment, or access to public services must remain subject to meaningful human oversight and appeal.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require public registers of AI systems used by government agencies with full transparency around AI use, including where in policy processes it has been used, and where or how it has been used to inform decisions. The party would ensure people are held accountable for AI decisions and that everyone has a right to challenge AI-assisted decisions, and to opt out of being subject to AI-assisted decision- making.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)
'Greens will regulate AI for the public good', 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Ensure AI does not replace human judgement or democratic decision-making

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that Artificial intelligence should support human judgement, not replace it, especially when it concerns warfare and the implications of that for the life and wellbeing of humans.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would refuse to purchase or deploy autonomous weapons systems and support an international ban on these, in the same way the international community has banned chemical and biological weapons.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)
'Greens will regulate AI for the public good', 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Refrain from purchasing or deploying autonomous weapons

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that while AI seems like a virtual technology, it actually consumes large amounts of resources, taking up land, using water to cool servers and requiring electricity to power data centres. This party says that any data centres based in New Zealand would need to follow strict regulations to protect the environment.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would require AI data centres to report on their environmental impact before being built. New facilities would be required to provide new renewable energy to cover their electricity use and their would be community consultation during the consenting process. To increase transparency, this party would require data centres to report their water use publicly.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Place limits on AI data centres' use of water and electricity

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that AI carries many risks, and can impact how information is understood. It says that news companies generate information and should be compensated by digital AI companies for how much information journalists generate ends up in AI summaries or responses.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would update and pass the Fair Digital News Bargaining Bill, requiring AI companies pay local media outlets for data used in their AI summaries.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Ensure news companies are paid by AI companies for their use of AI

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that AI companies can concentrate economic power, leading to bad outcomes for workers and individuals. These risks should be regulated by government.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would encourage the use of public-interest and open-source AI models wherever possible, and mandate the use of multiple and interchangeable AI models to prevent vendor lock-in. It would encourage the use of NZ-based and NZ-focussed large language models, rather than relying on AI tools from overseas companies.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Encourage the adoption of multiple types of AI

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that AI can concentrate economic power and impact individuals and communities. Power should not be concentrated, and the use of AI should not be at the expense of children and worker's rights.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would ensure children are not forced to use AI, especially at school, and broadly make sure that AI use around kids is in line with the UNCRC’s Joint Statement on Artificial Intelligence and the Rights of the Child. It would also require that workers are consulted about AI use in their workplace.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Protect children and worker's rights in the use of AI

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that people have a right to know when they are interacting with AI and how it is being used. AI content should always be clearly labelled so that people understand when they are using an AI model.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create labelling requirements for artificial intelligence, and audit algorithms for high-risk AI systems, so there is monitoring of AI use in the public sector. It would create an AI office within the department of prime minister and cabinet (DPMC) and aim to eventually establish an AI commission with independent powers to conduct audits assurance and education regarding AI use. This party would also collaborate with international best practice like the EU AI Act and build on NZ's work in the Christchurch Call to cooperate with like-minded countries regarding AI regulation and governance.

citations.title: 'Safe, sovereign AI. An AI Plan for Aotearoa' (PDF), 12 October 2026 (accessed 13 October 2026)

policies.statement: Create an AI office and require transparent AI use

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that students completing important jobs, like midwifery, nursing, social work and teaching, are required to complete paid work hours to receive their qualifications. These students must show up for as much as 30 hours a week, making it difficult to hold down another job. This party says that as NZ needs more of the people completing these qualifications, people on work placements should be paid, and supported if they are completing placements in other parts of the country.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would support students completing work placements for their study with a payment of $380 a week, on top of existing student loans or student allowances. Students who had to relocate for a placement (for example to a different region) would receive a one-off relocation payment of $1500.

citations.title: 'Greens announce paid placements for nurses, teachers, and social workers', 16 October 2026 (accessed 21 October 2026)

policies.statement: Pay students who need to complete work placements for their qualifications

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that for NZ's economy to get stronger, it needs a strong workforce. However, apprentice numbers are at a 15-year low. This party says that investing in people is a way to grow the workforce and economy and help apprentices to be supported in their chosen fields of work. Employers should also receive a financial incentive for supporting apprentices to complete their training.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would give apprentices a $2000 equipment grant for buying tools, equipment or uniforms required for their qualification. Employers who take on apprentices who finish their qualifications would receive $2000 when the apprentice finishes training.

citations.title:
'Green Party to abolish training wage and provide more support for apprentices
', undated (accessed 21 October 2026)

policies.statement: Provide $2000 to employers and apprentices to help with training

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that apprentice numbers are at a 15 year low, even though the ork apprentices do is important and needed. Low pay and insecure work prevent people from entering the trades, this party says. It wants to abolish the training wage, which allows apprentices or people in training to be paid less than the minimum wage for work they complete.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would abolish the training wage. All workers, regardless of training status, would be paid the minimum wage.

citations.title:
'Green Party to abolish training wage and provide more support for apprentices
', undated (accessed 21 October 2026)

policies.statement: Abolish the training wage

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that NZ needs more homes and renewable energy, and needs people who can do this work, such as builders nad electricians. However, apprentice numbers are at a 15-year low. It says that Māori and Pacific people face extra financial and structural barriers to completing training and this group should be supported specifically.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would create a $30m funding lift each year for Māori and Pasifika-led trades training. This will include pastoral care, job matches and wraparound services for newly qualified workers.

citations.title:
'Green Party to abolish training wage and provide more support for apprentices
', undated (accessed 21 October 2026)

policies.statement: Invest $30m in Māori and Pacific led trades training

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the NZ economy is important and must respond to the needs of New Zealanders, like good jobs and reducing emissions. It says the current Investment Boost scheme should be refocused on productive investments that create jobs with appropriate working conditions and low-emissions industries. As part of an overall jobs package, this party says this would create 284,000 jobs.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would refocus the "Investment Boost" government funding for businesses on businesses aligned with investment objectives, decarbonisation and good quality working conditions.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that it wants to protect at least 30 percent of NZ's oceans by 2030, including the Hauraki Gulf. It says this area around Auckland should be restored so biodiversity can flourish and people can swim and fish in the area.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value:
This party would commit to the goal of protecting at least 30 percent of the Hauraki Gulf by 2030. It would remove the ring-net fishing exemption from the Hauraki Gulf. 
This party says some of its other policies would also help the Gulf, including reducing bycatch with cameras on fisheries boats; resourcing iwi to lead ocean protection efforts; phase out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser and wastewater discharge limits to improve water quality and phasing out bottom trawling in significant areas and seamounts.

attributes.value: This party says that NZ's health system needs long term planning and funding to create good outcomes. To rebuild lost capacity, this party says further investment is needed. Under its fiscal plan, it would create long-term workforce plans and fund the health system further.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would increase public health funding by $3bn over four years, so the total would be $30bn spent on health by the end of that period. This money would go to long-term planning as well as immediate needs.

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that public investment is essential for economic development, productivity and resilience. This party says government investment can help grow NZ's economy and multiply impact later on. It says the government should increase revenue by creating a wealth tax, focusing on taxing capital and assets rather than productive work. Along with economic growth, this party says this plan will return the government to surplus while also creating better outcomes for New Zealanders.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would return the government to surplus by 2029/30. It would do this by increasing the tax base, prioritising taxing capital (i.e. a wealth tax) rather than labour.

citations.title: 'Green's Fiscal Plan builds real economic resilience to lower cost of living and stimulate 64000 new jobs', 23 October 2026 (accessed 27 October 2026)

policies.statement: Aim to create a government surplus by 2029/30

attributes.name: Why
attributes.value: This party says that the government can spend more money if it also creates a wider tax base, focused on taxing capital rather than assets. This party says the return to surplus should be delayed by a year because it is more important to focus on significantly increasing health funding. This party says that higher spending is a good investment for a government to make, along with changes to taxation.

attributes.name: How
attributes.value: This party would commit to government operating allowances between $4.5 to $4.7bn for the forecast period between 2026 and 2029/30. It would invest at least $3bn of additional funding in the health system per year. Extra operating allowances would also go to funding NZ's climate commitments, although this party says its preference is for climate goals to be met by lowered domestic emissions.
